newsitem.title: TOGO: Togo president seeks to promote dialogue in Niger.
newsitem.headline: Togo president seeks to promote dialogue in Niger.

text.p: Togo's veteran president, Gnassingbe Eyadema, is to send a team to Niger to promote dialogue among the different political players, officials said on Tuesday.
Eyadema took the decision after talks at his home village of Pya with Niger's president, Ibrahim Bare Mainassara, earlier in the day.
An eight-party opposition alliance accuses Mainassara of rigging a July presidential poll to legitimise his rule after a January 1996 coup.
Mainassara's supporters won a majority in the national assembly in a November poll boycotted by the main opposition.
Today, the three main opposition leaders, including Mahamane Ousmane, the civilian president Mainassara ousted, are detained and being investigated for threatening state security.
France and the United States, which has called Mainassara's election fraudulent, have urged their release.
Eyadema is chairman of the Entente Council, the region's oldest grouping, which dates back to 1959 and counts Togo, Niger, Ivory Coast, Burkina Faso and Benin as its members.
